editorial:
Imagine spending a relaxing weekend in the English countryside, only for everything to go sideways when people start dropping dead. You get to follow Lady Eileen Brent, a spirited flapper who doesn't let anything rattle her, and the charming Jimmy Thesinger. Together, they dive into a mystery that starts with a few weird deaths but quickly turns into a high-stakes game of spies and stolen government secrets. The whole vibe feels like a classic whodunit where you are constantly trying to figure out who is lying and what the secret society called the Seven Dials is actually planning.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the leads and the way the plot keeps you guessing. While the pacing is a bit slower in the middle, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love old-school mysteries with fancy clothes and clever dialogue, you will really enjoy this one. Since it is an older TV movie, you might want to look for a high-quality digital version.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that the Seven Dials is actually a group of patriotic citizens trying to stop a real spy ring from stealing government secrets. The deaths were part of a complicated cover-up to protect the mission. In the end, Lady Eileen and Jimmy uncover the true traitor among their circle. The bad guys are caught, the top-secret documents are saved, and the mystery of the Seven Dials is finally solved with everyone safe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Agatha Christie stories and British mysteries.
